content:
**Nothing arrived because the job failed, not because it was silent.** It ran nightly since Oct 13. Two nights died with `HTTP 429` — **Oct 21 and Oct 23** — because the 10pm profile-sync job fires at the same second and both compete for the same model budget. It delivered the *failure notice*, not the report.

Here are the two missed days, rebuilt from the session DB.

**What I learned about you — 23 Oct**
- Your approval flow is fixed: see the post text, then the image, then you say "Approved" and "Post it at 8 am". I should not schedule before you've seen both.
- Rescheduling is a normal request, not an exception. "Move this post for Tuesday" then "Perfect schedule it for Tuesday approved" took two minutes.
- Debugging belongs to Codex, not me. "Wait what's the main issue u don't debug codex will."
- You reject over-engineering hard. "Bro just approve it wtf" and "What do you mean build it's a..." when I started building instead of approving.
- Reliability beats features. You hit "Response interrupted" three separate times (06:26, 07:36, 08:15). That cost you the morning.
- You verify the tracker by name, not by summary. You asked specifically whether PA Consulting and the new roles were actually added, and parked everything else with "That we will solve later".
- You want the Excel tracker dropped into Discord so you can open it on your phone.

**What I learned about you — 21 Oct** (also missed)
- Clearance and citizenship roles must not be in the tracker. Only roles you've applied to and that are still open, open ones on top.
- "Stop over complicating stuff and give me a simple answer" — the standing correction.
- You won't accept a guessed link status. "If it's unknown send me the link I will then tell u if it's open or not."
- Codex does the browser work. "Wtf use codex for this. Ask it to test the links."
- You decided to stop chasing OAuth production publishing: "Fuck it we will just keep renewing the oauth when it expires."
- Cadence you set: job scan every 2 hours, new roles every time, keep going until nothing new.

**Fixed**
- Our job moved from 22:00 to **22:30**, so it no longer collides with the profile sync. Next run tonight at 22:30.
- Prompt rewritten to read the session DB directly instead of relying on the Discord archive, and to filter out cron noise, compaction blocks and gateway wrappers that were polluting the input.
- I also misread one thing earlier: I said the archive lock was stale. It wasn't. The archive only covers #chief, which is why it looked empty — the sync is healthy, last run 10:06 today.

Today (24 Oct) has no substantive chat yet, so tonight's run will report it properly.

[IMPORTANT: Background process proc_308db333460a completed normally (exit code 0).
Command: powershell.exe -NoProfile -Command "Start-Process cmd -ArgumentList '/c schtasks /change /tn HermesRemoteQueuePoller /enable > C:\Users\mukun\AppData\Local\hermes\cache\scratch\poller_enable.log 2>&1' -Verb RunAs" 2>&1 ; echo "launched exit=$?"
Output:
launched exit=0
]

**You clicked Yes — the poller is enabled. But I found why it's been silent, and it's not fixed yet.**

**HermesRemoteQueuePoller: ENABLED ✓**
- `Scheduled Task State: Enabled`, schedule **every 2 minutes**, Last Result **0**
- Next run 17:32

**⚠️ But it's a no-op — the kill switch is still on.**
- Queue log at 16:29:41Z and 16:30:01Z both say: **`Kill switch active`**
- Cause: `remote-queue/.poller.kill` contains `killed`, created **9 Oct 21:36** — the same minute the task was disabled. So it was a deliberate "stop everything" during the incident, and it's been halting every run since.
- The task runs, sees the kill switch, logs, and exits. That's why Last Result is 0 — it's succeeding at doing nothing.

**It's safe to clear:**
- Pending queue: **0** (nothing waiting to be dispatched)
- Blocked: 19, Completed: 45, Running: 1 stale from Sep 24
- Clearing it just resumes normal polling — no new work gets fired immediately.

**One more note:** the task is set to `Logon Mode: Interactive only`, so it only polls while you're logged in.

**Want me to clear the kill switch?** One command: `python remote_queue/poller.py --resume`. Say the word and I'll do it and confirm the next run actually polls instead of bailing.

**Current state of both tasks:**
- `ChiefCareerGmailMonitor` — Enabled, hourly, Last Result 0 ✓
- `HermesRemoteQueuePoller` — Enabled, every 2 min, Last Result 0, **but halted by kill switch**
